title: Rabies Deaths Expose Gaps Beyond Vietnam’s Household Gates
excerpt: A rabid dog attack in Đắk Lắk injured four people. Separate 2026 reports record 48 rabies deaths by 21 August, demanding stronger prevention and enforcement.
body_html:
In Đắk Lắk, authorities identified a dog with rabies after it attacked four people. That incident carries a hard medical truth: once rabies symptoms appear, disease is virtually 100% fatal. Read the reported case.

Household exposure incidents and commercial dog-trade risks are separate dimensions of one biosecurity challenge. A bite, scratch, or infected saliva entering broken skin or mucous membranes can transmit rabies. Meat that is properly cooked is not an established rabies transmission route. Handling sick animals, uninspected slaughter, and unsafe transport create different risks for handlers, veterinarians, families, and communities.

Every preventable exposure demands fast care

After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical assessment, even after delay. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes rabies vaccine and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Treatment must begin before symptoms develop.

Public health cannot stop at household gates

A Hải Phòng local-government notice reported 48 rabies deaths nationwide from the start of 2026 through 21 August. The notice urged stronger rabies prevention. Separate from those household and community incidents, illicit transport and uninspected slaughter can bypass quarantine controls and shift danger through populated areas. Each breach turns animals, workers, and families into unwilling participants in a preventable chain.

Vietnamese communities can demand a clean break

Local authorities already use measures such as registration, vaccination, leashes, muzzles, and holding facilities for roaming animals. Those safeguards need enforcement, transparent records, veterinary oversight, and protection for stolen companion animals. Public health targets belong to government policy. SDE’s campaign demand is clear: nationwide abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030.

Criminal networks profit when stolen pets, unsafe transport, and uninspected slaughter remain hidden. Vietnamese families, veterinarians, rescuers, and local leaders can reject that system together. Sign the national petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
